name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Kinetic Impactor Round KIR-10 'Hammerfall'
description: A heavy-caliber anti-materiel round designed for the Arcturus AM-10 platform that uses a two-stage propulsion system — conventional propellant for initial acceleration followed by a secondary rocket motor that ignites after 50 meters, boosting the 20mm tungsten penetrator to a terminal velocity that exceeds any conventional rifle round. The KIR-10 was designed to defeat next-generation reactive armor systems that use explosive countermeasures to deflect standard anti-materiel rounds — the rocket-boosted second stage arrives too fast for reactive systems to respond. Against personnel, the round is grotesquely excessive, but its use against augmented targets with military-grade armor implants has been documented.
specifications: caliber: 20mm tungsten penetrator stage 1: Conventional propellant, 600 m/s stage 2: Rocket motor ignition at 50m, terminal velocity 1,800 m/s effective range: 100-1,500 meters reactive armor defeat: Arrives before countermeasure activation magazine: 5 rounds in AM-10 platform round weight: 180g rifle weight: 14 kg propellant: Dual-stage — chemical + solid rocket
story_hooks: A KIR-10 round was fired through the engine block of an armored convoy vehicle, punching through both sides — the shooter was over a kilometer away and the reactive armor never triggered.
Arcturus is field testing KIR-10 rounds with a third stage — a terminal guidance package that allows the round to adjust course in the final 100 meters of flight.

Dramatic side-lighting from the left creates sharp shadows defining the ogival tungsten penetrator tip and emphasizes the material transitions between brass casing and anodized aluminum sections. The penetrator tip catches cool rim-light. Shallow depth of field keeps the round in sharp focus. Neo-noir urban aesthetic: cool color grading with slight teal tint in shadows, slight chromatic aberration at edges, subtle holographic lens flare suggesting military targeting systems. physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist cartridge with an aggressive, military aesthetic. The round presents as a massive cylindrical projectile with a pronounced ogival tip and a distinctly segmented body — the separation between conventional and rocket-boosted stages is visibly marked by a circumferential seam and heat-scorched aluminum ring. The entire assembly has the menacing geometry of purpose-built destruction.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 127mm. Bullet diameter (20mm tungsten penetrator): 20.3mm. Case length: 98mm. Rocket motor housing diameter: 22mm. Appears oversized even compared to other anti-materiel rounds.
physical_description.weight_description: Exceptionally dense and hefty — 180g creates a substantial feel despite compact form factor. The tungsten penetrator core loads forward weight, creating an unbalanced, nose-heavy impression that suggests kinetic power.
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten carbide penetrator core, brass composite case with embedded aluminum alloy rocket motor housing. Structural integrity reinforced with carbon-polymer sabot collar.
physical_description.finish: Satin brass casing with oxidized dark patches from manufacturing heat stress. The rocket motor section features a distinctive burnt-orange anodized aluminum collar. Tungsten tip has a gunmetal gray, slightly textured finish from tungsten carbide working.
physical_description.color_scheme: Burnished brass primary, charcoal-gray tungsten penetrator, burnt-orange rocket motor band accent. Subtle scorch marks and carbon streaking suggest field use or bench-testing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Not applicable — designed as a magazine-loaded projectile. The case neck features subtle knurling for loading assistance.
distinctive_features: Visible circumferential seam marking stage separation point at 50mm mark
Burnt-orange anodized aluminum rocket motor housing ring
Etched serial number array on case side (ADS-KIR10-5STAGE nomenclature)
Shallow concentric grooves around ogival tip for aerodynamic stability
Microscopic ablation scarring on penetrator tip from velocity testing
Hermetically sealed rocket motor ignition port (threaded brass plug)
Propellant charge inspection window on aft section (transparent polymer inlay)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo embossed on brass case at midpoint. Text reads: 'ARCTURUS KIR-10 HAMMERFALL | 20MM | DUAL-STAGE | MIL-RESTRICTED' in 2mm serif lettering. Serial batch code stamped in tiny characters on the aluminum rocket collar. NATO compliance marking laser-etched on penetrator.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-ready, pristine specimens show minimal wear; however, ammunition typically exhibits micro-oxidation on brass casings and slight polymer discoloration from thermal cycling in combat conditions. Storage marks from magazine compression visible on sabot collar.
